"See What Matters: Differentiable Grid Sample Pruning for Generalizable Vision-Language-Action Model" proposes the Differentiable Grid Sampler (GridS), a plug-and-play module that performs task-aware, continuous resampling of visual tokens in VLA models.

The paper addresses a fundamental trade-off in existing token pruning methods: aggressive compression using pruning inevitably discards critical geometric details like contact points, leading to severe performance degradation.

By adaptively predicting a minimal set of salient coordinates and extracting features via differentiable interpolation, GridS preserves essential spatial information while achieving drastic compression.

## Overview

RoboFlamingo is a vision-language manipulation framework built upon the open-source VLM OpenFlamingo, and it was presented as a poster at ICLR 2024.

## Key Features

RoboFlamingo utilizes pre-trained VLMs for single-step vision-language comprehension, models sequential history information with an explicit policy head, and is fine-tuned by imitation learning only on language-conditioned manipulation datasets. This decomposition provides RoboFlamingo flexibility for open-loop control and deployment on low-performance platforms.

## Performance

RoboFlamingo exceeds state-of-the-art performance with a large margin on the CALVIN benchmark. RoboFlamingo's architecture decouples vision-language understanding from decision-making and uses a simple policy head fine-tuned with imitation learning, proving to be a cost-effective and high-performance solution.

## Significance

RoboFlamingo can be trained or evaluated on a single GPU server and is proposed as a cost-effective and easy-to-use solution for robotics manipulation, making vision-language models more accessible for robotics applications.

Here are the search results for SparseVILA "Decoupling Visual Sparsity" ICCV 2025:

## Overview

SparseVILA is a new paradigm for efficient VLM inference that decouples visual sparsity across the prefilling and decoding stages. Vision Language Models (VLMs) have rapidly advanced in integrating visual and textual reasoning, but their scalability remains limited by the growing number of visual tokens that dominate inference latency.

## Key Approach

SparseVILA distributes sparsity across stages by pruning redundant visual tokens during prefill and retrieving only query-relevant tokens during decoding. This decoupled design matches leading prefill pruning methods while preserving multi-turn fidelity by retaining most of the visual cache so that query-aware tokens can be retrieved at each conversation round.

## Performance Results

Built on an AWQ-optimized inference pipeline, SparseVILA achieves up to 4.0 times faster prefilling, 2.5 times faster decoding, and an overall 2.6 times end-to-end speedup on long-context video tasks. Additionally, SparseVILA can retain higher context tokens resulting in a 5.9% margin over previous approaches in image-centric evaluation.

The paper appears to have been published at ICCV 2025 and is available through multiple sources including the official CVF conference proceedings and arXiv.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about LightVLA:

LightVLA is a simple yet effective differentiable token pruning framework for vision-language-action (VLA) models. While VLA models have shown impressive capability in executing real-world robotic tasks, their deployment on resource-constrained platforms is often bottlenecked by the heavy attention-based computation over large sets of visual tokens.

LightVLA addresses this challenge through adaptive, performance-driven pruning of visual tokens by generating dynamic queries to evaluate visual token importance and adopting Gumbel softmax to enable differentiable token selection, learning to preserve the most informative visual tokens while pruning tokens which do not contribute to task execution.

**Key Results:**
LightVLA reduces FLOPs and latency by 59.1% and 38.2% respectively, with a 2.6% improvement in task success rate.

**ICRA 2026 Acceptance:**
LightVLA has been accepted by ICRA 2026.

The paper (arXiv 2509.12594) was published on September 21, 2025, and the official code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/LiAutoAD/LightVLA.
